newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber closes mostly lower, cash market weak.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber closes mostly lower, cash market weak.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed mostly lower as the cash market continued to weaken, and active selling of September was linked to the liquidation of a producer long, floor sources said.
They noted Cargill Investor Services was a big seller of September, which closed $2.00 lower at $355.30 per thousand board feet.
Dealers said overall prices held up well, aided by strength in U.S. Treasury bond prices.
"We held up well after being limit down yesterday. There wasn't much followthrough (selling)," one floor trader said.
There was talk of trade in the cash market in the $345.00 to $350.00 range. Random Lengths earlier Wednesday reported a western spruce-pine-fir price of $355.00 per thousand board feet.
